body:
An ambient `RC_API_KEY` (e.g. exported in a shell profile) could take over even after an interactive OAuth login, and `auth status` misreported the active method — so writes failed on missing scopes with no clue why. Credential precedence is now explicit (`--api-key` flag → profile OAuth → `RC_API_KEY` → stored key), a conflict warns to stderr (kept out of `--json` stdout), errors name the missing scope and the credential's source, and `auth status --scopes` reports scopes best-effort.

Note: true fail-early on scopes needs a backend scope-introspection endpoint (`TODO(DX-940)`); API keys are opaque today.

DX-940

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which credential is sent on every API request and how login/status report auth; behavior is more predictable but wrong precedence could still block access until users adjust env or flags.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a case where an ambient **`RC_API_KEY`** could win over a profile **OAuth** login, so writes failed on missing scopes while **`auth status`** looked like the wrong credential was active.
> 
> **Credential resolution** is now explicit: **`--api-key`** → profile OAuth → **`RC_API_KEY`** → stored profile key. **`Config.Credential()`** reports the active token and source; **`--api-key`** is tracked via **`SetFlagAPIKey`** instead of overwriting stored keys.
> 
> When multiple credentials exist, the CLI **warns once** (stderr, including under **`--json`**) and **`auth status`** surfaces **`credential_source`** plus optional **`credential_conflict`** in JSON. **`auth status --scopes`** best-effort lists scopes from JWT claims; opaque API keys report **`scopes_available: false`**.
> 
> **API errors** name the missing scope when the message includes one, and hints mention whether the active credential came from env, flag, OAuth, or the profile. The API client stamps **`CredentialSource`** onto **`APIError`** for those hints.
>

DX-940 Auth: RC_API_KEY env silently overrides interactive OAuth; warn on conflicting credentials

From Cody's bug bash. A developer ran `rc setup`, completed the **OAuth** browser flow, but the CLI silently used an **under-scoped** `RC_API_KEY` exported in their `~/.zshrc` instead — so every catalog write failed, one missing scope at a time, and no project was ever created. Very confusing; the user had no idea a stray env var was in play. `rc auth status --json` during the session: ``` { "authenticated": true, "method": "api_key", "profile": "default", "project_status": "not_configured" } ``` ## Root cause (grounded in code) * `internal/config/config.go` `BearerToken()`: ```go if c.TokenType == "oauth" && c.AccessToken != "" { return c.AccessToken } return c.APIKey ``` If the profile lacks a usable OAuth token, it falls through to the API key. * On every load: `applyEnv(&cfg.envAPIKey, os.Getenv("RC_API_KEY"), &cfg.APIKey)` — `RC_API_KEY` from the environment is layered onto the profile. * `runtime.go:85` builds the API client from `BearerToken()`. * **There is no detection or warning when both a logged-in profile and** `RC_API_KEY` **are present.** The env key just wins by fallthrough, silently. ## Open question to confirm with a repro Cody's `rc setup` OAuth did *not* end up as the active credential (`method: api_key`, and `IsOAuth()` is checked first in `auth status`). Two possibilities — worth confirming by inspecting the saved profile: 1. `rc setup`'s OAuth didn't persist to the default profile (a setup bug), so `BearerToken()` fell through to the env key; or 2. It persisted but the ambient env key was still preferred somewhere in the flow. Either way the fix below stands. ## Fixes (Josh's asks) 1. **Precedence:** an interactive login you just completed (OAuth) should win over an ambient `RC_API_KEY`. At minimum, don't let an env var silently override a logged-in session. 2. **Warn on conflict (Stripe-style):** if both a stored/active credential and `RC_API_KEY` are present, say so loudly and state exactly which one will be used and where it came from (env var vs profile). 3. **Fail early on scope:** add `rc auth status --scopes --json` so an agent can see the key's scopes up front instead of discovering missing `project_configuration:*:read_write` one failed write at a time. When a write fails on scope, name the exact missing scope AND that the active credential is an env `RC_API_KEY` (so the user knows where to look). 4. `rc setup` **should announce the credential it's using** (method + source) before doing catalog work. ## Test plan * Profile has OAuth + `RC_API_KEY` set → OAuth is used (or a loud warning + explicit choice); `auth status` reports the truth. * `RC_API_KEY` set, no login → used, but `auth status`/setup name it as coming from the env. * `auth status --scopes` reports scopes; under-scoped key is flagged before any write. --- ## Implementation findings (fix branch `fix/dx-940-auth-credential-precedence`, local) The original root-cause framing was slightly off and is corrected here: * `BearerToken()` **already preferred OAuth** for real request auth, so the env key was NOT hijacking an authenticated session. The actual defects were: (1) `auth status` misreported the method (showed `api_key` even with a live OAuth token), (2) **no conflict signal** when two credentials were present, and (3) a real precedence bug where an explicit `--api-key` flag was outranked by a stored OAuth token. * **Precedence now implemented:** `--api-key` flag → profile OAuth → `RC_API_KEY` env → stored profile key. CI (env-only, no login) unchanged + tested. Conflict warning goes to stderr in all modes (survives `--json`; stdout JSON stays clean) plus a structured `credential_conflict` field in `auth status --json`. Errors now name the missing scope and the credential source (e.g. "came from the RC_API_KEY environment variable"). * **Open Q — does** `rc setup` **persist OAuth? YES.** `setup.go setupAuthenticate → loginWithOAuth → finishLogin → config.Save` writes `TokenType:"oauth"`. Persistence is not the cause. Most likely explanation for the report: a profile mismatch, or setup ran the non-interactive agent-prompt path (which never logs in) while an ambient underscoped `RC_API_KEY` quietly supplied a credential so nothing failed until scoped writes. * **Open Q — scopes: NOT readily obtainable.** No token-introspection / `me` endpoint returns granted scopes, and API keys are opaque. `--scopes` does a best-effort JWT decode of the access token and reports `null`/`scopes_available:false` honestly when it can't. Left `TODO(DX-940)`. **Follow-up: backend scope-introspection endpoint** would make true fail-early possible. Comment style: zero explanatory/slop comments added. Not pushed, no PR (will open as draft).
